summary: Trade policy and the Fed are the two risks that matter most. China formally opposes USTR's Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs (China +20%, plus Taiwan, Korea, Japan, the EU and India) but has not retaliated yet, and the Dec 9 hike is fully priced after a 3.3% core PCE. Oil risk is two-sided: Hormuz mine claims and Houthi strikes on one side, and on the other a possible OPEC+ rollover on Nov 29 with Brent near 3-month lows. AI governance headlines at Nvidia and the Dec 11 funding deadline are the next US-specific tests.

risks.title: Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs on 14 economies
risks.status: Nov 26: China's commerce ministry 'firmly opposes' the measures as unilateral and WTO-violating and reserves the right to respond (no countermeasure yet). Reuters: USTR intends to cap new tariffs at levels agreed in completed or pending deals (EU 15%), and European stocks rallied. Nov 25: USTR proposed tariffs on 14 economies (China +20% on top of the 2018 25%; also the EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India, Vietnam and others). Public hearings come first, so duties may not take effect until January
risks.market_pricing: Nov 25: Nasdaq 100 futures -3.2% pre-market, Kospi -6.16%, SOXX opened -5.8%; Nov 26: Europe +1.6% on the cap report; Asian chips bounced selectively (TSMC -0.2%)
risks.impact: Final rates at or above the proposals, or Chinese retaliation, would extend the semis de-rating and add to goods inflation (more Fed hikes); caps at deal levels or carve-outs after hearings would relieve Asian chip supply chains

risks.title: Fed hiking path (Chair Warsh)
risks.status: October core PCE 3.3% y/y (vs 3.2% expected, the highest since Nov 2023); Q3 GDP revised to 4.3%; Conference Board confidence 103.3. The Fed hiked in September and held at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike). The Nov 18 minutes said 'almost all participants' see further hikes as likely appropriate; Waller kept 50bp on the table. Bessent warned of overtightening. November jobs (expected Dec 4) is the last major print before Dec 9; November CPI comes after the decision
risks.odds: Dec 9 hike 100%, implied 4.15% (fed funds futures, Nov 25); FedWatch about 97% for 25bp and about 60% for another in January (via mlq.ai, Nov 25); Polymarket 25bp 87.5% / 50bp+ 9.3% (CryptoSlate mirror, undated snapshot)
risks.market_pricing: 13-week bill 4.155% (+47.7bp over 3 months); 10Y 4.848% (+81bp over 1 year, 98th 10-year pct on the monthly series); 10Y real 2.79%; futures price 4.355% by March
risks.impact: A hot jobs report or 50bp talk would push the 10Y back toward 5.3% and hit long-duration tech, small caps and housing; a 25bp-and-pause message would ease yields and extend the rotation into rate-sensitive groups

risks.title: AI trade: Nvidia governance, Anthropic IPO and AI-debt worries
risks.status: Nov 26: AP reports that S&P Global Ratings warned it could downgrade Nvidia over management and governance concerns. Moody's moved Nvidia's outlook to stable on Nov 18 after Huang's exit; the board reinstated Huang as CEO Nov 23, and an independent investigation plus a new export-control committee continue. Semis had their worst week since 2001 (Nov 20), then swung +15% / -9% / -6% on Nov 23-25. Anthropic (ANT) trades near or below its $83 IPO price ahead of MSCI inclusion Nov 30. Nvidia's general counsel testifies to House committees Dec 2. The FOMC minutes flagged opaque AI-related debt
risks.market_pricing: SOXX 127.98 (-41% from its 52-week high, -18pp vs SPY over 1 month); NVDA about $149, above its #1 VolumeLeaders level $126.60
risks.impact: A rating cut, hostile testimony or a credit event at an AI-debt borrower would push SOXX below 118.18; a calm testimony and stable ANT trading would let semis rebuild from support

risks.title: US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
risks.status: Nov 26: the IRGC says two tankers, one a supertanker, exploded after hitting mines north of Oman's Khasab (unverified; CENTCOM has called earlier claims false); the UN maritime chief says Hormuz remains unsafe; Trump says he is 'not rushing' on Iran until the new year. Since October the IRGC has made repeated mine-strike claims; about 14 attacks on vessels near Hormuz in the first 19 days of November (UK maritime count via Bloomberg). The US struck an IRGC site on Qeshm Island Nov 17; new US sanctions were reported Nov 24. Hormuz flows are reported near pre-war levels
risks.market_pricing: Brent 91.73, WTI 84.91, about 17-20% below a month ago; OVX 49.4 (79th pct); the market is fading unverified claims
risks.impact: A verified hit on Gulf export infrastructure or renewed large-scale strikes would send Brent back above $100 and add to inflation and hike pricing; a deal would push Brent toward the high $70s, helping consumers and transports and hurting energy and defense

risks.title: OPEC+ output policy (2027 quotas)
risks.status: All members meet virtually Nov 29 to set the 2027 framework; two delegates say a rollover of current targets is possible; Iraq and Kazakhstan want higher capacity baselines; the UAE is no longer in the group. EIA crude stocks +1.1M bbl (vs +1.5M expected). Gulf exports have run below normal because of the Iran war; Goldman's December Brent forecast is $105, the IEA sees a Q4 surplus
risks.market_pricing: Brent 91.73, near the bottom of its 89.37-117.64 3-month range; PVM sees $88-97
risks.impact: Higher 2027 baselines would extend oil's slide (bad for energy, good for inflation); a rollover with restraint would put a floor under oil

risks.title: China-Taiwan tensions, chip export controls and the US-China trade truce
risks.status: Early November: China massed more than 100 naval and coast-guard vessels in unannounced 'area denial' drills (Taiwanese official via Reuters); no named drills since. The Trump-Xi Shenzhen meetings (Nov 18-19) changed little on chips, rare earths or tariffs; China vowed countermeasures to the US AI-chip licensing rule. The truce runs to Jan 10; Trump and Xi are expected to meet again at the G20 in Florida in December. Taiwan and Korea added market-stabilizing measures after the chip rout
risks.market_pricing: SOXX -41% from its 52-week high; TSMC lagged the Nov 26 Asian chip bounce
risks.impact: Rare-earth curbs, probes of US chipmakers or named drills around Taiwan would hit semis first; a truce extension at the G20 or eased licensing would support a semis rebound

risks.title: US government funding (Dec 11) and the debt limit
risks.status: The September stopgap (House 370-48) funds the government through Dec 11. Leaders of both parties back another short-term stopgap past the lame-duck session; the new Democrat-controlled Congress is sworn in Jan 4. The debt limit could bind as soon as February 2027. 2025 had a 43-day shutdown and 2026 a 76-day partial shutdown
risks.impact: A lapse would delay data the Fed needs and dent Q4 growth; a clean stopgap into 2027 moves the fight to the debt limit under a divided government

risks.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping
risks.status: Nov 26: the Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and Riyadh's financial district (Reuters; damage unconfirmed). A Nov 22 claim of an attack on a Saudi refinery was also unconfirmed. Saudi Arabia warned Nov 6 that its Yanbu Red Sea hub could be targeted
risks.market_pricing: No visible premium; Brent near a 3-month low
risks.impact: A confirmed hit on Ras Tanura or Yanbu would be a major oil shock; unconfirmed claims keep being faded

risks.title: CMS anti-fraud rule for managed care (Medicare Advantage)
risks.status: CMS proposed an anti-fraud rule (CRUSH) on Nov 18; UnitedHealth fell about 18% over five days. XLV has since recovered (+1.39% over 5 days, +14.3pp vs SPY over 3 months). The comment period is under way
affected: Quality health care theme (JNJ, MCK, LLY)
risks.market_pricing: XLV -0.56% Nov 25 but leading over 3 and 6 months
risks.impact: A broad final rule would cut managed-care margins; a narrowed rule would let the group extend its leadership

risks.title: Israel government formation after the Oct 27 election
risks.status: Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) got the mandate Nov 8 with 67 endorsements; the 28-day window ends around Dec 6 (extendable by 14 days). Disputes over Ra'am and the ultra-Orthodox parties persist; his bloc is reportedly preparing a minority-government vote before Dec 6 and he has floated a 'national emergency government'. Failure could hand Netanyahu another try or lead to a new election by early 2027
risks.impact: An Eisenkot-led government would likely be more cautious on Iran (mildly bearish for oil and defense); a failed mandate extends caretaker uncertainty while strikes on Iran are debated

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine war and peace talks
risks.status: US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11) produced a large prisoner swap but no breakthrough; US envoys then met Putin in Moscow. Russia still demands all of Donbas, which Kyiv rejects; Witkoff said Europeans will join the next round, but a Kremlin aide said Moscow has not agreed (Nov 16). Strikes continue
risks.odds: Ceasefire by Dec 31 9.5%, by Mar 31 2027 23.5% (Polymarket via Rio Times, early Nov)
risks.impact: Real progress would be mildly bearish for defense and European gas and good for European equities; a collapse keeps the defense theme supported

risks.title: Japan: weak yen, intervention risk and BOJ pressure
risks.status: Mid-November: the yen neared 160 per dollar; Finance Minister Mimura warned of intervention risk, and PM Takaichi said Tokyo is in close contact with US authorities. The Takaichi government has nominated dovish BOJ board members
risks.market_pricing: DXY 103.77, near the top of its 3-month range
risks.impact: A sudden intervention or BOJ hike could unwind yen carry trades and hit high-beta tech (as in Aug 2024); a stable yen keeps it a background risk

risks.title: Brazil after Lula's re-election
risks.status: Lula won the Oct 25 runoff 51.76% to 48.24% over Flávio Bolsonaro; the real and Brazilian stocks had their sharpest falls in years on fiscal-spending fears; Bolsonaro challenged the result, and the electoral court confirmed it
risks.market_pricing: The real fell as low as 5.60 per dollar after the vote, then pared to about 5.40
risks.impact: A fiscal blowout would weigh on EM sentiment; a credible budget would let Brazilian assets recover; little direct effect on the watchlist
